The farm which was opened in 1897*08 has now^^P®”™®*: practically become a potato seed farm and in 1918 grew* OTer 1,000 mannds of seed for distribution. In connection with the cattle stock improvements it may be mentioned that of the stock imported in 1902 and 1903, those which came from Patna have proved the better breed.

Pure bred Patna bulls are being sold at the nominal rate of B-s. 60 each to Khasis for breed- ing purposes. Tho introduction of English and Austra- lian pigs in 1902 has proved a failure, but Dumba rams imported to improve sheep have proved a fair success. The experimental fruit garden started in 1902 has not proved a success and the site was abandoned in 1902 as a fruit garden and handed over to the Eoman Catholic Mission as a Scricultural farm, as it contains a largo number of mulberry trees. A new fruit garden on a more favourable site on the Jowai road was opened in 1913 and shows every sign of success. The tropical plantation opened in 1904i at Wahjain has not proved a success and was abandoned in 1911 as the site was 2 found ■anstiitable and tte soil too poor. Experimonts ■were made with tea on the high plateau in 1904. At» tempts have also been made to introduce the oultiva'tion of silk.

Seed of the univoltine worm was procured from Erance. and the experiment proved successful but the Elhasis do not seem inclined to take to sericul- ture. One or two individuals and the Koman Catholic Mission are however continuing the work and it is possible that in time the industry will spread. FORESTS. At Nongpoh a cook and a khit- matgar are now maintained at the D0.k Bungalow and a tea house has recently been constructed by the road side for the convenience of travellers. A daily service of motor-cars and lorries between Shillong, Gauhati and Pandughat has replaced the old tonga Service and connects up with the Eastern Bengal State Hailway. The journey from Shillong to Calcutta aud vice vend is now performed in a little over 24 hours. Shillong was constituted a station under Act V (B.O.) of 1876 in 1878 and afterwards converted into a Miudcipality' under Act III of 1884 in November 1910. Its affairs are managed by a Committee of 16 members presided over by the Deputy Commissioner. The principal sources of revenue are a tax on houses at 7i per cent, of their annual rental, water and latrine rates and a grant from Government.

The Dhaleswari, the Karnafulli and the Sonai are the rivers in the hills that are used as routes for traffic. Boats of fifty maunds burden can proceed up the former river as far as Sairang even in the cold weather. The passage up-stream is very slow, in the cold weather a boat with a load of fifty maunds generally taking three weeks for the journey from Silchar to Sairang while an empty boat takes about eight days. In the rains the voyage is often twice as long. At that season of the year it generally takes a boat a week to negotiate the 6| ■ miles of roaring torrent that separates Ohangsil from Sairang. A boat carrying ten maunds or so can however, do the voyage from Salchapra to Sairang in ten dap in the cold weather and in about sixteen to twenty in the rains. The Sonai was used during the scarcity in 1911 and 1912 to boat up rice from the plains. The Dhaleswari, the Karnafulli and the Sonai are the rivers in the hills that are used as routes for traffic. In the rains the voyage is often twice as long. At that season of the year it generally takes a boat a week to negotiate the 6| ■ miles of roaring torrent that separates Ohangsil from Sairang.
